colophon.title: How this site is built
colophon.body:
This portfolio is a macOS clone (iOS on mobile), hand-coded end to end — no template.

The base: Nuxt 3, Vue, TypeScript and Tailwind. Animations run on GSAP: draggable windows, dock minimizing, scroll reveals (ScrollTrigger).

The apps are real: Weather queries open-meteo with the visitor's location, the Calculator actually computes, Messages runs my home-made chatbot, Spotlight (⌘K) navigates everywhere, and the App Store GitHub stats are live.

System sounds are synthesized with Web Audio (zero audio files), icons are hand-drawn SVG or Framework7 Icons (MIT), and the boot screen is server-rendered to avoid any flash.

Three languages, clean SEO, verified build. The code says the rest.

digitaleo.title: What I'm learning at Digitaleo
digitaleo.body:
Two and a half years of apprenticeship on a real SaaS product used daily — that shapes you.

The most formative part: the email editor. Making an email look right in Outlook means diving into VML and conditional HTML — a world without modern standards. I shipped dynamic blocks, the preheader, an emoji picker, mobile column reordering.

Another lesson: living with legacy. Reusing Vue.js Design System components inside AngularJS screens instead of rewriting everything teaches you to create value without breaking what exists.

Around the code: GitLab CI/CD, feature flipping, demanding code reviews, daily collaboration with Product Owners and designers in Figma.

stack.title: My 2026 stack
stack.body:
Front: Vue and Nuxt first — that's where I'm most productive. TypeScript everywhere, Tailwind for speed and consistency, GSAP when things need to move well.

Back: Node.js, PHP at Digitaleo, MongoDB and PostgreSQL depending on the project. Prisma and Auth.js on my recent Next.js projects (Mosaic, TailTCG).

Tools: Docker, GitLab CI/CD, and Claude Code, which changed how I work — this portfolio is the proof.

Right now: the AI & Data Master's at Epitech is pushing me toward machine learning. The logical next step.
